newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends steady, back months up.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends steady, back months up.

text.p: CSCE nearby active world sugar futures ended little changed Monday, but back months continued to post gains, hitting new life of contract highs, as the coming season is likely to see a decline in world sugar production as consumption climbs, analysts said.
"There was a lack of buying in the front month, and the spreads remained under pressure, as speculative support was attracted on the open and the close," one trade house broker said.
CSCE October sugar ended off 0.02 cent at 11.26 cents a pound, after trading a 11.22-11.34 cent range, with resistance still seen near the contract highs at 11.40 cents.
The October/March spread went further into contango, ending around 0.23 cent a pound, after remaining in backwardation around 0.10 cent a pound until late June.

But the October contract's five-day moving-average moved back up above its 21-day average Monday for the first time since May, while the 21-day average remains above the contract's 55-day average, suggesting the contract remains in a slow uptrend.
Twenty-day historical volatility has also been increasing slowly, rising over 20 percent in the past week, from 10 percent in early June.
And the March 1997 contract saw a new contract high at 11.53 cents, before ending up 0.03 cent at 11.50 cents.
"Sugar prices continue to trend slowly higher," Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka said.
"Part of the increase appears to be due to expectations that world stocks of sugar will decline in the 1997-98 season," he said.
"But sugar supplies still look more than adequate and a good crop in Europe could actually pressure the market."

World ending stocks on August 31, 1997 are forecast to be 48.4 million tonnes, up from 46.7 million the year before, according to industry statistician F.O. Licht, the third year in a row that world stocks will increase, as production continues to more than match rising demand.
